analysis.title: UBS Daily Consumer/Lux 04 Nov: M&S (+ve), Ahold (-ve), CCH (+ve), Barry Callebaut (mixed)
key_insights: Markets opened weak for tech-exposed names after Democrats won both chambers of Congress. Nasdaq futures fell as much as 2.4% before recovering to about -50bps for Nasdaq and the S&P. EStoxx opened -50bps and was already about 1% off its lows.

The desk reads the move as a sharp rebuke of Trump and a narrower legislative runway, not a growth scare. The dollar was the cleanest expression: USDJPY back below 158, CHF +0.5%, EUR and GBP higher. Gold rose about $50 to about $3,980/oz and the UST 10yr eased 2bps to 4.94%.
KOSPI rallied 4% off the lows back to unchanged, which suggests market pricing was more in line with odds markets on the midterm results.

AI earnings cushioned the tech selloff. AMD, ANET, ALAB and SMCI beat with stronger outlooks on AI/data-center demand. SWKS sold off on weak post-Qorvo guidance and FRSH fell on softer billings and a modest FY trim. VRNS beat but withheld guidance because of its pending acquisition.

China trades higher (CSI300 +3%, SHCOMP +1.9%, regional semis +10%) on state support measures. The services gauge unexpectedly dipped for the first time since July. October A-share new account openings fell -21.5% MoM (-35% YoY), so retail appetite is cooling.

Oil is steady with WTI around $96 as the US and Iran pursue diplomacy despite limited American strikes. The API showed a crude draw of -5.3m and distillates -1.2m, with builds in gasoline (+1.4m) and Cushing (+0.5m).

Marks & Spencer (UBS Buy) 1H adjusted PBT of £403m was modestly ahead of consensus. A material FH&B (fashion, home and beauty) margin miss was offset by strong Food profitability. FY27 PBT is guided in line with market expectations, and focus shifts to FH&B margin recovery in H2.

Ahold Delhaize (UBS Neutral) beat in 3Q, with underlying EBIT about 4% ahead of consensus and both US and Europe better. A cyber incident forces a FY26 downgrade: €75-100m Q4 EBIT hit, margin now approaching 4.0% (below the 4.0% consensus), FCF cut to about €2.1bn from at least €2.3bn.

CCH (UBS house broker, Buy) beat on 3Q organic volume and sales and is the only EU beverages company to raise topline guidance again through Q3 earnings season. Organic EBIT guidance is unchanged at 8-10% because of cost pressures including Ukraine supply chain disruption.

Barry Callebaut (UBS Neutral) FY26 core EBIT fell -15.6% y/y to CHF594m, in line with consensus. FY27 guidance is volume +1-3% and core EBIT +3-5% (CHF610-625m versus consensus CHF627m). UBS reads consensus earnings as in line with guidance, marking the end of the negative revision cycle, and expects no material consensus changes. A Hershey contract is in discussion.

Unilever (UBS Sell) confirmed its medium-term algorithm (4-6% underlying sales growth, at least 2% volume growth, modest margin improvement) and said 2027 will be consistent with it. Consensus is already there. A new €1bn productivity programme runs to the end of 2029 and more than offsets €400-500mn of stranded costs from the Foods separation.

Pandora (UBS Neutral) beat strongly on 3Q like-for-like (LFL) sales, led by the US, Europe and APAC/Japan. FY26 guidance was narrowed toward the upper end, and 2027 and mid-term margin targets were raised on improved silver hedging. Q4-to-date LFL is +1%, with lower promotion a drag and an underlying trend of +3%. The UBS salesperson expects the shares to rise today.

Part of Pandora's 3Q margin beat was one-off: a partial refund of its US IEEPA tariff claim added 340bp to gross margin and 370bps to adjusted EBIT margin. Underlying EBIT margin was broadly flat y/y.

Keurig Dr Pepper (UBS Buy) beat in 3Q, aided by $99M of tariff refunds, but shares traded -4% on US Coffee concerns, a soft pod category, and a cut of about 1pt to legacy KDP EPS growth. UBS expects US Coffee to return to growth in 4Q and sees the stock at a -26% discount to the group.

UBS argues the US aftermarket auto thesis (ORLY, AZO) is supported by an aging fleet, professional repair share gains and pricing power. The margin debate is shifting to diesel, wages, healthcare and IT costs.

US softlines: if the Iran conflict ends, UBS ranks GAP, UAA, CRI, GIII and PVH best positioned for estimate-revision upside. KSS and DBI are high-beta beneficiaries but have already rallied. OXM, RL, TPR, GOOS and REAL offer less residual event alpha. Rankings are for one-to-three-month moves and 12-month ratings are unchanged.

Luxury: Ferrari's order book reaches into 2028 and the Luce is fully covered for 2027. UBS notes luxury-sector valuations remain near cyclical lows. Hugo Boss (Neutral) EPS was cut -11%/-2%/-2% and UBSe EBIT is about 7% below consensus for FY27 on freight and raw material costs. Brunello Cucinelli (Buy) faces a founder-related news story in China and South Korea that UBS treats as a risk, not an earnings event, until consumer reaction is evidenced.

European retail positioning: the sector is short skewed. TSCO is the most crowded long and JMT the most crowded short in food, NXT the most crowded long and HMB the most crowded short in fashion. UK grocery competition data show Aldi/Lidl share at about 19.1% with industry space growth subdued, supportive for Tesco and Sainsbury's.

Earnings previews: Intercos (5 Nov), Diageo Q1 (5 Nov), Orkla (6 Nov), Henkel (10 Nov), WOSG H1 (10 Nov), Burberry H1 (12 Nov), Richemont Q2 (13 Nov), Edgewell and YETI (12 Nov), plus Spectrum Brands. UBS is ahead of consensus on Intercos, Henkel, Diageo, Richemont and WOSG-type strength, and in line on Burberry, Altria and YETI.

sector_views.rationale: UBS favors GAP, UAA, CRI, GIII and PVH for unrecognized estimate revisions if the Iran conflict ends. KSS and DBI could be high-beta beneficiaries, but their rallies lower confidence.
Aging fleet (average used vehicle sold 11.6 years old), professional repair share gains and healthy pricing power. ORLY and AZO are favored.
Sector valuations remain near cyclical lows and Ferrari demand is strong, but Hugo Boss faces freight and raw material pressure and demand is described as softer and more volatile for many peers.
The sector is short skewed. Food and hardlines positioning improved versus a month ago and fashion was less negative.
CCH is the only EU beverages name to raise topline guidance again through Q3 earnings season, though CCEP faces Europe volume risk into FY27.

earnings_insights: Marks & Spencer 1H (reported 4 Nov): group underlying PBT £403m versus Visible Alpha consensus £398m and UBSe £388m. Food EBIT margin 5.6% versus consensus 5.1%. FH&B EBIT margin 7.5% versus consensus 9.6%. FY27 PBT guided in line with consensus (VA £939m, UBSe £920m).

Ahold Delhaize 3Q (reported 4 Nov): EBIT €946m versus company-compiled consensus €910m and UBSe €890m. Margin 4.1% versus 4.0% consensus. US comp sales +0.5% versus +0.3% consensus. Europe comp sales +2.1% versus +1.3%. FY26 guidance cut: underlying operating margin now approaching 4.0%, underlying EPS growth low single digit at constant FX (was mid-to-high single digit), FCF about €2.1bn (was at least €2.3bn), on an estimated €200-250m Q4 sales and €75-100m operating profit hit from the cyber incident.

CCH Q3 (reported 4 Nov): organic volumes +5.4% and organic sales +9% versus consensus +4.8% and +8%. FY26 organic sales guidance moved slightly above the 6-7% range (consensus +7%). Organic EBIT guidance reiterated at 8-10%. Net finance cost guidance lowered to €35-45m from €40-50m, supporting about 1% upside to FY26 consensus EPS.

Barry Callebaut FY26 (reported 4 Nov): volumes -0.7% y/y to 2,110K tonnes (UBSe 2,114k, consensus 2,106k). Core EBIT CHF594m (UBSe CHF599m, consensus CHF594m). Core net profit CHF216m (UBSe CHF220m, consensus CHF212m). EFCF CHF2,010m versus consensus CHF1,776m. FY27 guide: volume +1-3%, core EBIT +3-5% implying CHF610-625m (consensus CHF627m).

Pandora 3Q (reported 4 Nov): group LFL +4% versus company-compiled consensus and UBSe +2%. Gross margin 83.7% versus consensus 80.3%, including a 340bp one-off from a partial US IEEPA tariff refund. Adjusted EBIT margin 15.9% versus consensus 13.1%, including +370bps from the refund. 2026 guidance narrowed: organic sales growth +2-3%, LFL 0% to +1%, EBIT margin 22.5-23.0%. 2027 EBIT margin target raised to 14-15% including one-offs and 15.5-16.5% excluding.

Keurig Dr Pepper 3Q (reported): beat on stronger top line and margins, including $99M of tariff refunds. Core FY26 guidance reiterated, legacy KDP EPS growth cut by about 1pt. Shares -4% at time of writing.
Yum China Q3 (reported): revenue US$3,477mn (+8% y/y, +2% ex-FX), net profit US$311mn (+10%), restaurant margin 17.8%, SSSG -3%. Quarterly dividend US$0.29 per share.
Sysco 1Q (reported): cleared its 2.5% local case growth target. EPS in line with the company's expectations for the period. Shares pulled back 9%.
Yonghui Q3 (reported): revenue Rmb11.5bn (-8.3% y/y), net loss Rmb83m, recurring net loss Rmb33m versus Rmb699m in Q325.

Upcoming (UBS estimates, not printed): YETI 3Q26 on 12 Nov, UBS forecasts EPS $0.85 versus Street $0.85, GM 56.5% versus Street 56.8%. WOSG H1 (10 Nov) UBS forecasts sales £954m and EBIT £82m. Edgewell F4Q26 on 12 Nov before the open. Burberry H1 (12 Nov) and Richemont Q2 (13 Nov) previews are in line and ahead of consensus respectively.

trade_ideas.description: Long GAP, UAA, CRI, GIII and PVH as the best-positioned US softlines names if the Iran conflict ends
trade_ideas.rationale: Best mix of incremental earnings upside, inexpensive valuation, positioning, and limited apparent discounting in the stock price.
trade_ideas.risk: Conflict outcome is uncertain. KSS and DBI have already rallied, and the framework favors unrecognized estimate revisions over obvious thematic exposure.

trade_ideas.description: Long ORLY and AZO as the strongest ways to capture the US auto aftermarket opportunity
trade_ideas.rationale: Aging vehicle fleet, professional repair share gains, heavy investment in inventory and distribution, and healthy pricing power.
trade_ideas.risk: Margin debate shifting to diesel, wages, healthcare and IT costs, and consumer pressure may delay some repairs.

trade_ideas.description: Stay Buy Keurig Dr Pepper after the post-earnings drop
trade_ideas.rationale: US Coffee expected to return to top-line and operating income growth in 4Q, USRB performance best in class, and the stock trades at a -26% discount to the group.
trade_ideas.risk: Sentiment hinges on US Coffee performance in the near term, with a soft pod category.

trade_ideas.description: Buy Sysco on the 9% post-1Q pullback, $95 price target
trade_ideas.rationale: UBS thinks the pullback was overdone and execution remains on track, with inflation picking up quarter to date.
trade_ideas.risk: Restaurant Depot case growth slowdown and softer-than-expected enterprise inflation.

tension_points.what_invalidates: The Iran conflict not ending, or estimate revisions failing to materialize.
